title: Rec.709 Export Looks Lighter in QuickTime? Check the Viewer
description: A Rec.709 export can look lighter in QuickTime than in an editor because their viewing pipelines may interpret gamma and display color differently.
direct: A Rec.709 export can look lighter in QuickTime than in an editor because their viewing pipelines may interpret gamma and display color differently. Compare the identical file under consistent conditions before changing the grade or converting it again.
figureAlt: A single media file and editor/player cards illustrate a consistent viewing check.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export.
cards.choice.heading: First isolate playback
cards.choice.body: Use one saved file, not a source preview on one side and a social-media transcode on the other. Keep display brightness and viewing conditions stable. A different appearance does not by itself prove that HDR tone mapping failed.
sections.explain.heading: A viewing mismatch is a separate problem
sections.explain.body: Adobe documents QuickTime gamma differences for Premiere exports and provides viewer-gamma choices. The correct workflow depends on your editor, display and delivery specification. Do not apply a random compensation LUT to every export or assume one appearance will match all screens.
sections.practice.heading: Keep the conversion claim precise
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops VideoFix for iPhone. It converts HDR to Rec.709 SDR in an H.264 MP4, with three free conversions before purchase. This creates an SDR delivery copy; it is not a claimed QuickTime gamma-repair tool or a manual gamma-tag editor. Rec.709 gamut, transfer functions and player interpretation are related but distinct. The illustration represents a same-file viewing check, not a measured display comparison.

steps.step-1.text: Confirm whether the saved file is HDR or already Rec.709 SDR. Keep the original and inspect the export’s color tags in a trusted editor.
steps.step-2.text: Open that same export in the editor and intended receiving player. Check the editor’s display color management and viewer gamma settings.
steps.step-3.text: If an HDR source genuinely needs SDR delivery, create a separate Rec.709 copy with VideoFix, then inspect that copy in the destination workflow.
